title: RBAC v2 migration orchestration playbook and integrity monitor
creator: Ayesha Raman
description: Orchestrate a staged migration from RBAC v1 to RBAC v2 with automated integrity checks, a minimal-risk customer canary path, clear rollback guards, and baked-in audit-log continuity and SSO group mapping validation. Deliverables: migration playbook, integrity monitoring service (consistency-checker), customer comms templates, and on-call runbook for incidents.
updates: 2025-01-20 — Kickoff alignment: agreed to a phased approach (canary cohort -> org waves -> bulk) rather than an immediate cutover. Key trade-off: longer migration window vs reducing blast radius.

2025-01-27 — Team decision: implement dual-write for 7 days per org in canary, then switch to read-from-primary with asynchronous reconciliation. Rationale: reduces latency impact while enabling verification; avoids long-lived dual-write complexity.
2025-02-05 — Prototype: consistency-checker v0 validates role mappings for canary orgs (delta detection, drift alerts). Found 2 user-group mapping edge cases from SAML attribute gaps.

2025-02-12 — Security review: list of required audit fields confirmed (actor_id, prev_role_set, new_role_set, mapping_source, saml_assertion_hash). Security suggested preserving RBAC v1 IDs in audit payloads for traceability.
2025-02-18 — Customer comms draft reviewed by Legal and Support. SLA language adjusted to clarify the expected short window for role re-evaluation and timelines for manual fixes.

2025-02-24 — Ops: on-call playbook added. Emergency rollback plan tested in staging — canary org restored to RBAC v1 state via toggled feature-flag and backfill reconciliation run succeeded within 12 minutes.
2025-03-01 — Pre-cutover checklist complete for wave 0 (internal + five pilot customers). Scheduling cutover for pilot orgs on 2025-03-05 with 48h observation window.
2025-03-02 — Post-migration telemetry: consistency-checker reported <0.02% mapping drift after initial dual-write window; two SAML mapping fixes queued (ENG-14310, ENG-14311).
Notes: Updated at 2025-03-02 by Marcus Li.
acceptance_criteria: Playbook published in Confluence and reviewed by Security, Privacy, and Support
Consistency-checker deployed to prod with alerting (pager duty) and dashboard showing per-org drift metrics
Canary cohort migration completed with rollback tested and documented
Audit log schema preserved and verified for continuity across RBAC versions
Customer comms templates approved and staged for wave rollouts
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: SAML group attributes missing leads to incorrect role mapping. Mitigation: validate SAML mappings pre-migration and mark affected orgs as manual-review; include fallback logging of SAML assertion hash for post-mortem.

Risk: Long-running dual-write causes inconsistency under retries. Mitigation: keep dual-write window short (7 days max per org), implement idempotent writes and monotonically increasing version tags on role objects.

Risk: Audit log discontinuity breaking compliance reports. Mitigation: embed v1_role_ids and v2_role_ids in every migration audit event and run a reconciliation job that emits compensating events if gaps are detected.
Risk: Customer-facing outages during rollouts. Mitigation: canary small set of low-risk orgs first; implement traffic-split and feature-flag toggle to instant-roll-back the v2 read path.
Risk: Unauthorized elevation due to mapping bug. Mitigation: pre-cutover smoke tests for privilege escalation vectors and post-cutover automated penetration checks focused on role boundaries.
runbook_steps: Preflight: run SAML attribute completeness script against orgs and tag 'manual-saml-review' where attributes are insufficient
Step 1 (Canary): enable dual-write for pilot orgs and start consistency-checker; monitor 'role-drift' alerts for 48 hours
Step 2 (Verification): run reconciliation job and verify audit logging contains both v1 and v2 role IDs for migrated events
Step 3 (Wave rollouts): enable v2-read path behind feature-flag for wave orgs; keep dual-write enabled for wave for 24-72 hours based on stability
Step 4 (Bulk backfill): run asynchronous backfill with rate limits; use monotonic version tags to ensure idempotency
Emergency rollback: flip feature-flag to route reads/writes to RBAC v1, schedule reconciliation run to repair any transient inconsistencies, notify customers and support
qa_plan: Unit tests for mapping logic and idempotent dual-write codepaths (coverage target 95% for mapping module)
Integration tests: end-to-end SAML group mapping using sampled customer assertions; include replay tests for retries and failures
Staging canary run with synthetic traffic that exercises common and edge-case permission checks
Load test: simulate expected production write/read load for 2x burst for 30 minutes to validate latency SLOs under dual-write
customer_communication_snippets: Week-of notice: We will begin a phased migration of our permission system to a new, more flexible model. During your org's migration window we will run automated checks; no action is required unless you receive a manual review request.

Pilot completion note: Your org was included in the pilot migration on 2025-03-05. We detected no unauthorized changes. If you notice any unexpected access changes, please contact support@redwood.ai and we will prioritize a rollback.
Support escalation template: include affected user IDs, observed role before/after (v1_id / v2_id), SAML assertion hash (if applicable), and relevant request IDs
